title: Zorb Learns Why $100 Buys Less Every Year
description:
Zorb, a very confused alien, finds out why Earth snacks cost more every year. Inflation means prices rise across the whole economy, and Earth's central bank actually aims for a little of it on purpose. Figures: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI for the 12 months ending September 2026, and the Federal Reserve.

Education, not financial advice.

#Shorts #inflation #personalfinance

beats.line: Your snacks cost more every year and nobody on Earth is surprised. Why?
Same snack. Bigger number. Earthlings call this inflation.
Official Earth example: a basket that cost 100 dollars now costs 107. That is 7 percent.
Same money. Smaller basket. Very sneaky, Earthlings.
In the latest 12 months, Earth prices rose 3.7 percent.
Twist: Earth's central bank wants inflation. Its goal is 2 percent a year.
Not zero. Two. On purpose. Zorb is still processing.
Zorb will return. Earth money remains confusing.
